entry.title: How I Built an Animated Circle Progress Component Using FSCSS (No JavaScript)
entry.summary:
Most circular progress indicators require JavaScript or heavy libraries. I wanted something lighter. So I built a Circle Progress plugin for FSCSS that generates animated radial progress components using pure CSS and custom properties. The result is a reusable component that can be customized with simple classes. Demo The Idea The component uses a conic-gradient to draw the progress arc and a radial mask to turn it into a ring. A small glowing dot follows the arc to give it a dynamic UI feel. All the logic is wrapped in an FSCSS plugin: @circle-progress() the circular arc animated glow dot progress value display customizable colors responsive sizing First include FSCSS. Then initialize the plugin. @import(exec(_init circle-progress)) Create the progress component:
72%
Set the value with FSCSS: .p72 { @progress-range(72) } Customizing Colors You can create color variants easily. .blue { --progress-color-arc: #4d9fff; --progress-color-glow: rgba(77,159,255,0.45); } Example:
45%
Changing Size You can scale the component using a helper. .big { @progress-size(260px) } Example:
72%
FSCSS allows reusable CSS logic using @define and @use. Instead of repeating complex CSS, the entire component becomes a single reusable function. @define circle-progress(selector){ ... } This makes it easy to build UI components purely with CSS preprocessing logic. https://github.com/Figsh/Circle-progress.fscss/

Generative AI models are powerful, but they have an important limitation: they only know what they were trained on.
